title: Evaluation Bridge for Quant Migration and Deployment Playbook
author: Ayesha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the "evaluation bridge": a repeatable, auditable process that connects the eval-harness outputs, probe telemetry, and runtime shadowing to a safe quantized model migration and production rollout. It is intended for ML engineers, release engineers, and SREs running mixed-precision or integer quantized deployments on Redwood Dedicated and Private fleets.

Why this doc exists
-------------------
- Quant migrations reduce cost but introduce subtle quality regressions (coherence, factuality, functioncall fidelity).
- Cross-system signal mismatch (eval harness vs. runtime telemetry vs. shadow) is the primary source of blind rollouts.
- The evaluation bridge defines gating criteria, telemetry alignment contracts, and operational runbooks to make quant migration deliberative and reversible.

Scope
-----
This playbook covers:
- Candidate selection and candidate instrumentation for quant evaluation (offline/hybrid).
- Shadow and bridge-run orchestration templates.
- Telemetry alignment: key metrics, tolerances, and drift detection.
- Rollout decision matrix and rollback triggers.
- Example configs, CLI snippets, and ownership.

Definitions
-----------
- Bridge run: a scheduled or ad-hoc hybrid evaluation that mirrors live traffic to a candidate quant model with stored probes and limited live sampling.
- Probe cohort: curated set of prompts (production prompt families + synthetic stress probes) used to anchor quality checks.
- Delta budget: allowed percentage or absolute change for a metric between baseline (float) and candidate (quant) before gating fails.

When to use the evaluation bridge
--------------------------------
1. When promoting a model variant that uses a new quant profile (per-workload or new library).
2. When moving from mixed-precision to lower-bit quant for cost reasons.
3. Prior to canary or A/B rollout of quant artifacts on Dedicated or Private.

High-level flow (one-line)
-------------------------
select candidate -> bake probes & shadow config -> bridge-run (hybrid) -> compare metrics against gates -> canary -> phased rollout or rollback

Decision matrix (simplified)
----------------------------
- Required pass to continue to canary: all hard gates pass.
- Optional (but recommended): soft gates pass and monotonic drift trend absent for 72h.

Gating rules (hard/soft)
------------------------
- Hard gates (must pass):
  - Functional failure rate <= baseline + 0.5% absolute (for critical endpoints).
  - Regression in functioncall fidelity (if used) < 1.5% absolute measured by functioncall correctness probes.
  - Latency P95 delta <= +25 ms or +10% (whichever is smaller) for same batch config.
  - No new deterministic crashes or decoding failures in 100k sample shadow.
- Soft gates (weight for decision):
  - Coherence score (holistic eval) delta <= 2.0 points on task-specific scale.
  - Embedding cosine drift across probe cohort <= 0.015 mean.
  - Tokens-per-response variance increase <= 12%.

Telemetry alignment contract
---------------------------
The bridge run must produce telemetry from the same instrumentation used in production and the eval harness. Required telemetry fields:
- request_id, tenant_id (anonymized), route, model_variant, probe_id, seed_bucket, latency_ms, token_count, decoding_errors, embedding_vector_hash, functioncall_result_hash, quality_score_{intent,factuality,coherence}

Telemetry export frequency: 1m aggregates + full-event stream to the eval-store for sampled requests.

Bridge-run orchestration (steps)
--------------------------------
1. Candidate registration
   - Register quant artifact in model registry with a unique model_variant tag (e.g., model-x-quant-v3).
   - Attach quant-profile metadata: algorithm, bits, per-channel-scaling, calibrated-fp16-fallbacks.
2. Probe cohort assembly
   - Compose a probe cohort: 60% production-seeded probes, 30% edge-case synthesized probes, 10% randomized perturbations.
   - Label probes with expected invariants (must-return_json, must-include-entity, length-bucket).
3. Shadow wiring
   - Configure shadow rule: route 100% traffic to baseline (float) and mirror 5% traffic to candidate in async mode OR run offline replay of sampled production traces.
   - Ensure request headers include bridge-run markers: X-Bridge-Run: <id>, X-Seed-Bucket: <n>.
4. Hybrid evaluation execution
   - Run the eval-harness on assembled probes against baseline and candidate with N seeds (default N=5 for stochastic models).
   - Simultaneously run shadowed live traffic capture for 48-72 hours (adjust by workload).
5. Aggregation & alignment
   - Aggregate event stream and eval outputs into a bridge report. Perform metric alignment and normalization (tokenization differences, sampling seeds).
6. Decision & next steps
   - If hard gates pass -> promote to canary (document canary scope).
   - If hard gates fail -> abort and escalate to quant-team triage.
   - If soft gates fail -> extend bridge-run (additional probes/shadow) or perform targeted fine-tuning of quant-profile.

Operational thresholds and examples
----------------------------------
| Metric | Baseline | Allowed delta (hard) | Allowed delta (soft) | Measurement window |
|--------|----------|----------------------|----------------------|--------------------|
| Functional failure rate | 0.6% | +0.5% abs | +0.25% abs | 100k requests |
| Latency P95 | 210 ms | +25 ms or +10% | +15 ms | 24h rolling |
| Coherence score | 78.0 | - | -2.0 points | probe-run |
| Embedding cosine | 0.872 | -0.015 mean | -0.010 mean | probe cohort |

(Note: tables in Confluence should be created from the above CSV; here we present a textual rendition.)

Rollout checklist (pre-canary)
-------------------------------
- [ ] Bridge report uploaded and linked to model registry entry.
- [ ] SLO owner sign-off (quality, latency, cost tradeoff).
- [ ] Canary scope defined (percentage, region, tenant selectors).
- [ ] Runtime fallback policy configured: immediate fallback to baseline on decoding_errors or crash.
- [ ] Observability dashboards created and default alert thresholds set.
- [ ] Runbook and oncall rotation assigned (see Ownership & SLAs).

Rollback triggers (automatic)
---------------------------
- Latency P95 for canary exceeds baseline + 50 ms for 15m sustained.
- Functional failure rate exceeds baseline + 1.0% abs over 30m.
- Critical customer error spike normalized to >5x baseline for any tenant for 10m.
- Unrecoverable decoding_failure rate > 0.1% on the canary stream.

Ownership & SLAs
----------------
- Bridge owner: ML Infra / Quant Team (primary) - pager duty escalation to quant oncall.
- SREs: ensure shadow throughput and telemetry export (SLA: 99.9% export success for sampled events).
- Product/PM: approve the canary scope and customer-facing risk appetite.

Example bridge config (YAML)
---------------------------
# bridge-run.yaml
model_variant: "model-x-quant-v3"
quant_profile: "per-channel-int8-calibrated"
bridge_id: "bridge-20260517-az1"
probe_cohort: "probe-cohort-202605-a"
shadow_mode: "async-mirror"
mirror_percentage: 5
hybrid_run: true
seed_repeats: 5
metrics_window_minutes: 60
hard_gates:
  functional_failure_abs: 0.5
  latency_p95_ms_delta: 25
soft_gates:
  coherence_points: 2.0
  embedding_mean_drift: 0.015

CLI snippets
------------
# register candidate
redwoodctl model register --name model-x --variant model-x-quant-v3 --artifact s3://redwood-artifacts/model-x/int8-v3.tar.gz --meta quant_profile=per-channel-int8-calibrated

# start bridge run
redwoodctl bridge run --config bridge-run.yaml --output /tmp/bridge-reports/bridge-20260517-az1.json

# collect report
redwoodctl bridge collect --id bridge-20260517-az1 --destination gs://eval-store/bridges/

Telemetry analysis guidelines
---------------------------
- Normalize token indexing between baseline and candidate using the same tokenizer version before computing embedding drift.
- Use bootstrap sampling for coherence and functioncall correctness (N=1000 resamples) to establish confidence intervals.
- Stitch together eval-harness synthetic probes and live shadow samples by seed_bucket tags for aligned per-slice comparison.

Triage rubric for failures
-------------------------
1. Repro: attempt to replay failed probes in the quant sandbox with identical seeds. If deterministic failure reproducible -> create P0 for quant-team.
2. Isolated degradation: if degradation localized to a slice (e.g., system prompts containing dates), create a patch probe set and run incremental tuning of scaling tables.
3. Systemic shift: if drift present across probes and shadow samples, revert candidate, open a postmortem, and plan either model float re-tuning or alternate quant profiles.

Appendix: common troubleshooting notes
-------------------------------------
- Tokenization mismatches are the most common false-positive for embedding drift. Confirm tokenizer versions in artifacts and runtime.
- Small per-channel calibration errors can cause entity hallucination; if seen, inspect calibration dataset and increase calibration set size by 3x.
- If latency regresses but quality is preserved, consider per-route quant routing (route heavy QPS to quant, sensitive routes to float) as an interim.
